chunks: And what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ahmad ibn Hamzah, from Aban, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
«The grandfather shares equally with the brothers, until the one-sixth share is better for him.»

key_terms.الْجَدُّ: The grandfather (specifically paternal in this context)
key_terms.يُقَاسِمُ: He shares/partners (implies equal division of the residue)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a paternal grandfather when full brothers are present?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific mechanism of 'qismah' (equal division) between the paternal grandfather and full brothers, a key point of contention in Shia jurisprudence. It establishes that the grandfather is not merely a residual heir but competes directly with brothers, taking the greater of the two calculated shares (equal portion vs. fixed one-sixth). This ruling underscores the principle that the grandfather's proximity to the deceased grants him a status comparable to brothers in the absence of parents, reflecting the nuanced application of Quranic inheritance verses.
